reason: While the text contains multiple named characters (Isaac, Esau, Jacob, and Rebekah), they cannot be accurately characterized as 'regular people.' These are biblical patriarchs and matriarchs who hold foundational significance within the Abrahamic covenant tradition. They are portrayed as key figures whose actions and lineages determine the destiny of nations—Isaac as a patriarch of the covenant line, Rebekah as his chosen wife, and Jacob and Esau as the progenitors of Israel and Edom respectively. The narrative itself emphasizes their sacred status through the blessings invoked and the divine significance attributed to their lineage. While they are depicted with human characteristics and everyday concerns (preparing food, family deception), they occupy an exalted religious and historical position that places them far above the status of ordinary people.
